message.content:
The famous scene where Del Boy falls through the bar is from the episode **"Yuppy Love"**, which was the first episode of **Series 6** of *Only Fools and Horses*. It originally aired on **8 January 1989** on BBC1.

In this iconic scene, Del Boy (played by Sir David Jason) and Trigger (played by Roger Lloyd Pack) are in a trendy wine bar trying to impress two women. Del tells Trigger to "play it nice and cool, son, nice and cool," but as he goes to lean on the bar, he doesn't notice the barman has lifted the counter hatch — and falls straight through to the floor. Trigger then looks around wondering where Del has gone.

This scene has frequently been voted the funniest moment in British sitcom history. Interestingly, it was almost different: writer John Sullivan originally wanted Del to simply stumble and catch himself, based on a real-life incident he'd witnessed. However, David Jason insisted on falling all the way through, drawing on his experience in stage farces. Additionally, Trigger wasn't originally meant to be in the scene — Roger Lloyd Pack apparently turned up unannounced on the filming day, and John Sullivan decided to include him, with Trigger's bemused reaction adding to the comedy.
